newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar posts modest gains vs yen by late Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Dollar posts modest gains vs yen by late Tokyo.

text.p: The dollar racked up gains against the yen by late trade on Tuesday due to growing speculation the Group of Seven (G7) nations may not take any concrete steps to rectify the dollar's strength at their weekend meeting.
"There is doubt whether even Japan will strongly voice concerns about the dollar's rise against the yen (at the meeting)," said a dealer at a major trust bank.

A senior dealer at a U.S. bank in Tokyo said the latest dollar buying spree originated from remarks by prime minister Ryutaro Hashimoto on late Monday when he expressed doubts about the possibility of lowering the value of the dollar.
"Is it possible to lower the value of the dollar through international cooperation? I don't think that's the feeling at the moment," Hashimoto said.

Meanwhile, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a news conference on Tuesday that Japan does not welcome an excessive sharpening or weakening of the yen. But many traders turned a deaf ear to his remarks.
